    Yaxel Lendeborg’s parents are Yissel Raposo and Okary Lendeborg, both former basketball players for the Dominican Republic national team who provided a strong athletic foundation for the Michigan Wolverines star. His mother, Yissel, is widely credited with guiding his career, forcing him to pursue college basketball despite hardships, and is currently battling cancer. 
    • Mother (Yissel Raposo): A former two-sport athlete (basketball and volleyball) in the Dominican Republic and the American University of Puerto Rico. She was crucial in turning Yaxel’s life around by pushing him toward Junior College and frequently supported him during his 2026 NCAA tournament run despite her cancer diagnosis.
    • Father (Okary Lendeborg): Played basketball at a high level for the Dominican Republic national team. He worked, while Yaxel was often with his mother, who served as a primary mentor.
    • Family Background: The family moved from Puerto Rico to Pennsauken Township, New Jersey. Yaxel is known for his close, grateful relationship with his parents, particularly his mother, whom he has described as the "strongest woman" he knows.
    • Support & Motivation: Yaxel frequently cites his mother's influence as the reason he is currently playing, telling The Players' Tribune that she "saved [his] life" when he was struggling to find his path.

    For Yaxel Lendeborg, basketball was always about having fun. She was working the angles like crazy behind the scenes. Just doing her Dominican mom thing and hustling to find a way for everything to pay off for me. Making phone calls. Sending emails.
